rationale: The ground-soybean adjunct comparison gives longer ON and less dyskinesia. The abstract does not separate resting tremor or compare refined oil.
Spirography improved after both active octanol formulations. The pooled adverse-tremor and inconsistent six-hour results cannot isolate soybean oil.
Only the drug comparator varies against a shared oil vehicle. The prespecified essential postural tremor timepoint was inconclusive and later signals favor the drug.
Acoustic voice measures favored the active drug over the soybean-oil placebo. No oil-free placebo identifies a soybean oil effect and the refining grade is unspecified.

At day seven, 2.1 versus 4.7 (estimates read from Figure 4a) in highest oral whole-plant methanol-extract versus vehicle groups, eight mice per group. Fresh petioles carry identified extract compounds. Their effective dose and mediation in the mouse trial are unresolved.
The fresh petiole analysis found apigenin and luteolin also measured in the experimental extract. Chemistry supports an exposure link and supplies no independent symptom result.

Pharmaceutical butylphthalide compared off-medication tremor pooled across three types. The purported composite exceeds the stated maximum and nearly reproduces a quality-of-life row. The separate rest result cannot be interpreted.
One public contributor reported previous tremor, uncertain diagnosis and general benefit with seed extract, coffee and mannitol. No tremor change was attributed to a single exposure.

Two prints of one cohort's turkey frequency versus pooled self-reported tremor graphic. The tile is extremely close to zero on the positive side. Cooking, separate rest item, adjusted estimate, uncertainty and analyzed denominator are unverified.

Tremor returns in qualitative Figure 2 and 3 timelines after protein challenge in two participants. The third revised-load participant has no figure and the lower-load comparison has a different protocol. The authors give no specific rest score or baked exposure.

Six diet-alone participants and ten assigned the same fig-containing diet plus bowel cleansing. Preparation and individual consumption are missing. Motor totals, including Figure S2, do not provide a separate resting-tremor contrast.

A concentrated fruit extract reportedly favored general motor measures in haloperidol-treated rats. The available author abstract gives no item-level rest tremor estimate or active-exposure bridge to raw fruit. Keep full methods open.

Methods identify two bark formulations in 18 rats at assignment. Tables 11–13 are biochemical and have unclear analysis denominators. Discussion of a fruit-extract catalepsy result does not establish that arm in the experiment.
Groups of six per test received an aerial-part extract. Alertness and spontaneous activity fell, and rotarod time shortened. The assays lack a Parkinson or resting-tremor outcome.

A modern review lists Anjir and phenolic compounds as a potential Parkinson-related plant. Reference 20 leads toward fruit chemistry with bibliographic inconsistencies. No firsthand remedy or symptom outcome is available.

Three fresh fig cultivars had measured phenolics. The chemistry connects the traditional review's candidate reference to raw fruit, while there is no measured mediator match to the rat experiment or efficacy outcome.

Two copies of one graphic for the same cohort give a small inverse tile for unspecified olive oil and pooled self-reported tremor. There is no pairwise estimate, uncertainty, grade or separate rest item. The 2017 composite symptom analysis overlaps and has no separate tremor result.
Exact oil grade administered by injection improved rotarod and activity under toxin exposure. An acute tremor observation was outside the comparative endpoints.
The ketogenic recipes use extra-virgin olive oil. During the early phase, 12/24 versus 3/23 reported worsened tremor or rigidity. This is a bundled diet comparison with a combined adverse endpoint.
The oil association addresses Parkinson case status, with no within-disease separate tremor estimate or confirmed grade.

Table 2 shows one attenuation in ten tremor reports and prose mentions transient worsening without a count. The study selected volunteers; preliminary report overlap and separate rest outcomes remain open.
Named authors describe mustard among pungent dietary items and propose a general link to shaking. There is no firsthand treatment response.
Appendix A lists mustard within a menu. No ingredient comparison or separate rest result is reported.
Registered total scale and related white-seed enzyme formulation trail. Clinical use of the exact formulation and outcomes remain unverified.
An isolated compound with a registered total motor scale, unknown overall status and no posted results. There is no culinary-comparator premise.
Unheated brown powder added to cooked broccoli changes urinary metabolite recovery in healthy adults.
Measured raw and roasted black seed chemistry. Total glucosinolates fell. Preexisting isothiocyanate results were inconclusive.
Original bar, grip and coordination figures assess leaf extract. No rest-tremor rating or culinary seed comparison.
Relative glucosinolate signals declined after roasting. No measured Parkinson symptom or preparation-equivalent human dose.
The processed mustard adjunct raises measured urinary sulforaphane metabolite recovery. The study has no human Parkinson or rest-tremor outcome.

Sixty-one people randomized to isolated caffeine or placebo. UPDRS III rest tremor differed by -0.32 (95% CI -0.73 to 0.10) and -0.28 (-0.83 to 0.27) at weeks three and six. Both timepoints use the same trial. Tea chemistry confirms caffeine in the beverage with substantially smaller amounts per reported serving.

A caffeine dose escalation without an external comparator gives a within-group rest score reduction of 1.18 points at two weeks. Tremor worsening and physiological tremor occurred among discontinuation reasons. Twenty-five participants described, with substantial attrition.

Six percent of survey respondents with Parkinson perceived worse tremor with coffee. The same publication reports no clear increase after acute caffeine and does not give a separate compatible rest estimate. Group linkage and timing are unresolved, so no additional family count was assigned.

Brewed black tea averaged about 39 mg caffeine per 200 mL in cup-sized bags and 24 mg for loose leaf under those conditions, compared with 200 or 400 mg daily isolated caffeine in the clinical trial. Measured constituent bridge, with no symptom observations.
Some LRRK2 groups had favorable MDS-UPDRS II composite comparisons. The idiopathic comparison was inconclusive and a separate rest-tremor estimate was unavailable.
